place_fields.summary: A major Subrahmanya pilgrimage centre in the Western Ghats, associated with serpent worship and Sarpa Samskara rituals.
place_fields.best_time: October to March; early morning is preferable for a quieter visit

planning_attributes.description: Kukke Shri Subrahmanya Temple is a Hindu pilgrimage temple at Subrahmanya in Dakshina Kannada, dedicated to Lord Subrahmanya and strongly associated with serpent worship.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Dakshina Kannada district tourism records the traditional association of Vasuki and other serpents taking refuge under Subrahmanya; the site is especially known for Sarpa Samskara.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The district administration places Kukke about 104 km from Mangaluru by road; Subrahmanya Road is the nearest rail connection and Mangaluru is the nearest major airport.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Follow temple dress, worship and photography rules; ritual-specific access can differ from general darshan.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Heavy monsoon rain can affect roads and nearby Western Ghats routes; check local conditions before travel.
planning_attributes.notes: A pilgrimage-focused destination; nearby Subrahmanya-area sacred sites can be combined in the same visit.

place_fields.summary: Historic hill temple in Kadri known for Manjunatha worship, an important bronze Lokeshwara image, natural springs and nearby caves.
place_fields.best_time: October to March; early morning or late afternoon

planning_attributes.description: Kadri Manjunatha Temple is a historic temple on Kadri Hill in Mangaluru, dedicated to Manjunatha, a form of Shiva.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The Dakshina Kannada district administration describes Kadri as an 11th-century temple site with natural springs and laterite caves; the site also has documented Buddhist and Natha traditions.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The temple is in Kadri, Mangaluru, around 2 km from the city centre according to the Dakshina Kannada district administration.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Follow temple-specific dress, worship and photography rules on arrival.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The hill and cave surroundings can be slippery during heavy rain; use care on wet surfaces.
planning_attributes.notes: Nearby Kadri Hill, natural springs and the historic cave area make the temple suitable for a short heritage stop.

place_fields.summary: A prominent Mangaluru temple dedicated to Gokarnanatha, noted for its Chola-style architecture and its central role in Mangaluru Dasara.
place_fields.best_time: October to March; mornings or festival periods for cultural activity

planning_attributes.description: Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Kshetra is a Mangaluru temple dedicated to Gokarnanatha, a form of Shiva, and is closely associated with Narayana Guru and Mangaluru Dasara.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The temple's history page states that Narayana Guru consecrated the Shiva Linga in 1912 and that the temple was transformed into a Chola-style structure in 1991.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The temple is in Kudroli, about 2 km from central Mangaluru; its history page lists about 2.7 km from Mangaluru Central railway station and 12 km from Mangaluru International Airport.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Follow temple-specific dress, worship and photography rules on arrival.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Crowds can become substantial during major festival events; allow extra time for access and parking.
planning_attributes.notes: The temple is a major cultural stop in Mangaluru and the focal point of Mangaluru Dasara celebrations.
